newsitem.title: USA: No significant rain seen for U.S. Midwest corn.
newsitem.headline: No significant rain seen for U.S. Midwest corn.

text.p: Farmers in parts of the U.S. Midwest are expected to see high temperatures and no significant rain for the next seven days, further stressing a corn crop now in the pollination stage, meteorologists said.

"There appears to be no significant rain for the dry areas of central and southern Illinois, parts of central and southwestern Indiana, eastern Missouri and eastern Iowa for the next seven to ten days," Weather Services Corp meteorologist Mike Palmerino said.
"This weather will continue to raise concerns about this year's corn production in those states," Palmerino said.
But Palmerino noted readings will not be excessively high over the next week for Illinois, Indiana, Iowa and Missouri.
"High temperatures this weekend will range from the middle 80s to middle 90s (degrees Fahrenheit)," Palmerino said.
The cooler weather is expected during the first half of next week with highs mostly in the 80s F, he said.
Palmerino predicted the highest reading for Springfield, Ill., this weekend to be 95 F.
But he forecast a few light showers of under 0.25 inch rain in those areas which likely would not improve soil moisture conditions.

Weather Express Inc chief forecaster Fred Gesser said on Thursday rains would be confined to west Texas, New Mexico, Colorado Rockies and western Plains of Kansas up to western and west central Nebraska and southeastern South Dakota.
"The precipitation is expected to be locally heavy in many of those areas with about 70 to 80 coverage with one half inch or better," he said.

For Friday, Gesser forecast rain showers over northeast Nebraska, northern quarter of Iowa and extreme southern Minnesota. "Those showers should make it to Madison (Wis.) and Milwaukee but won't reach central Illinois," he said.

"The next chance of rain in the Corn Belt should come on Saturday and Sunday across South Dakota, southern Minnesota, extreme northern Iowa, southern Wisconsin, Michigan, northeast Indiana and northern half of Ohio," Gesser added.
He expected 0.25-1.5 inch rain with 30 to 40 percent coverage for those areas.
But Gesser noted a cold front would be heading toward central Illinois, bringing some potential rain on August 6.

"I am comfortable in forecasting 0.50 to 2.00 inches of rain and 70 percent coverage for Iowa on August 5 to 6," Gesser said. "I am less confident for significant rain coverage for central and southern Illinois on August 6."
The hottest days for the Corn Belt (eastern Kansas, Missouri, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana and Ohio) would be Sunday, Monday and Tuesday, Gesser said.

"Peoria should be no more than 91 to 92 (degrees F) for that period of time," Gesser said. "So it will be a little bit cooler than the previous weekend where temperatures soared to 95 and over," he said.
